name: Finnish postal code
doc: Postal code (postinumero) in Finland: five digits. Helsinki codes start with 00.

name: Finnish individual tax number (veronumero)
doc: Veronumero, the 12-digit tax number given to people who work in the construction industry in Finland. It is separate from the personal identity code and holds no personal information.

doc: Y-tunnus (yritys- ja yhteisötunnus, in Swedish FO-nummer), the business identity code of companies and organisations in Finland: seven digits, a hyphen and a weighted check digit.

name: Financial Instrument Global Identifier (FIGI)
doc: The Financial Instrument Global Identifier (FIGI) (formerly Bloomberg Global Identifier (BBGID)) is an open standard, unique identifier of financial instruments that can be assigned to instruments including common stock, options, derivatives, futures, corporate and government bonds, municipals, currencies, and mortgage products.

name: Finnish identity card
doc: The Finnish identity card is one of two official identity documents in Finland, the other being the Finnish passport.

name: File name extension
doc: Suffix of a file name that tells the format of the file, such as pdf, docx or csv, written with or without the leading dot. The full name of a file is the datatype filename.

name: FIPS 10-4 country or region code
doc: Two-letter code of a country, optionally followed by two characters for a first-level subdivision, from the US standard FIPS 10-4, withdrawn in 2008. Some datasets, such as GDELT, still use it.

name: FIPS 5-2 numeric code (US states)
doc: Two-digit identifier for US states and other associated areas per former Federal Information Processing Standard FIPS 5-2 standard

name: FIPS 6-4 numeric code (US counties)
doc: Identifier for US entities (mostly counties) per "Federal Information Processing Series" (FIPS 6-4), used for counties, Puerto Rico zona urbana, Metropolitan Statistical Areas (MSA) and Combined Statistical Areas (CSA) in the United States.

doc: Indian first name by known name identifier

name: Flight number
doc: In the aviation industry, a flight number or flight designator is a code for an airline service consisting of two-character airline designator and a 1 to 4 digit number.

name: FlyBase ID
doc: Identifier of an object in FlyBase, the database of Drosophila genes and genomes: FB, two letters for the kind of object and seven digits. Gene identifiers start with FBgn.

name: Micronesia postal code
doc: Postal code in Micronesia: a ZIP code of five digits from 96941 to 96944, optionally followed by a space or hyphen and four more digits.

name: Faroese V-number (Vinnutal)
doc: V-tal (Vinnutal), the number that the Faroese Tax Administration (TAKS) gives to businesses. It is the tax identification number of legal persons in the Faroe Islands. It is a six-digit consecutive number, sometimes written with an FO prefix.

examples.description: Example from the python-stdnum documentation, written in groups

name: Formal Public Identifier (FPI)
doc: Structured text identifier from SGML (ISO 8879 and ISO/IEC 9070) used in DOCTYPE declarations of SGML, HTML and XML documents. It consists of an owner identifier, a double slash and a text identifier. The owner starts with -// (unregistered), +// (registered) or ISO. The text identifier starts with a public text class such as DTD or ENTITIES, followed by a description and, after another double slash, a language code.

examples.description: The public text class is missing

name: Formal title
doc: Title of rank, honour or office written before a person's name, such as Sir, Dame, Lord, Lady, The Honourable or His Excellency. It is more formal than a common title such as Mr or Mrs (civility).

examples.description: man with a British knighthood or a baronet
woman with a British knighthood in her own right
The Honourable, used for some officials and judges

name: Fully qualified domain name (FQDN)
doc: Complete domain name of a host or zone, written as labels separated by dots from the host up to the top-level domain, such as www.example.com. A trailing dot stands for the DNS root and is left out in most data. Each label has 1 to 63 letters, digits or hyphens and does not start or end with a hyphen, and the whole name has at most 253 characters (RFC 1035, RFC 1123). Internationalized names are stored as Punycode labels that start with xn--. The regexp requires at least two labels and rejects an all-numeric last label, so IPv4 addresses do not match.

examples.description: Decentralized identifier (DID); a colon is not allowed in a label
URL; a domain name has no scheme or path
A label that ends with a hyphen
IPv4 address; the top-level label must not be all-numeric

ru.name: Полное доменное имя (FQDN)
ru.doc: Полное доменное имя узла: метки через точку до домена верхнего уровня, например www.example.com.

name: French education region code (académie)
doc: Two-digit code of an académie, the regional district of the French Ministry of Education, as used in the national directory of schools (field code_academie), for example 01 for Paris. Some numbers are no longer used after académies merged, such as Caen and Rouen into Normandie (70). Other ministry nomenclatures use three digits.

name: French functional urban area code (INSEE aire d'attraction des villes)
doc: Three-character code of an aire d'attraction des villes (AAV), the INSEE 2020 zoning of a city and the communes from which many people commute to it. Files name the column aav2020. Communes outside any area can carry a special value instead of a code.

ru.name: Код зоны притяжения города Франции (INSEE AAV)

name: French departmental arrondissement code (INSEE)
doc: Code of an arrondissement, the subdivision of a French department, in the INSEE Official Geographic Code (COG) - the department code followed by one digit, 3 characters in metropolitan France and 4 in overseas departments. Municipal arrondissements of Paris, Lyon and Marseille have commune-like codes (fr_arrondissement_municipal_code).

name: French municipal arrondissement code (INSEE)
doc: INSEE code of a municipal arrondissement, which exist only in Paris (75101 to 75120), Marseille (13201 to 13216) and Lyon (69381 to 69389). The codes have the same form as commune codes and are used in place of the commune code in many statistical files.

name: French living area code (INSEE bassin de vie)
doc: Five-character code of a bassin de vie, the smallest INSEE zoning in which residents have access to the most common services and facilities. The 2022 zoning has 1,707 living areas, 26 of them overseas; files name the columns bv2022 or bv2012 after the zoning year.

name: French canton code (INSEE)
doc: Code of a canton in the INSEE Official Geographic Code (COG) - the department code followed by two digits, 4 characters in metropolitan France and 5 in overseas departments. The COG also lists pseudo-cantons (canton-ville) that group whole communes, numbered from 99 downwards, and fictitious cantons for communes nouvelles, numbered from 89 downwards.

name: French legal category code (INSEE catégorie juridique)
doc: Code of the legal form of a legal unit in the INSEE nomenclature of legal categories, used in Sirene as categorieJuridiqueUniteLegale. The nomenclature has three levels - 1 digit (9 positions), 2 digits (37 positions) and 4 digits (260 positions); Sirene uses the 4-digit level, for example 5710 for a simplified joint-stock company (SAS).

examples.description: Société à responsabilité limitée (sans autre indication)

name: French CEDEX address line
doc: Last line of a French address for the CEDEX service (Courrier d'Entreprise à Distribution EXceptionnelle) of La Poste for organisations with large mail volumes - a 5-digit CEDEX code, the name of the delivery office in capitals and the word CEDEX, sometimes followed by a one- or two-digit number. Sirene splits it into a code (codeCedexEtablissement), which looks like a postcode, and a label.

examples.description: the number has at most two digits

name: French legislative constituency code
doc: Code of one of the 577 constituencies that elect the National Assembly - the department code followed by a two-digit number, as in the official election results of the Ministry of the Interior. That file writes department codes without a leading zero (101 for Ain 1re); other publishers pad them (0101). ZX is used for Saint-Martin and Saint-Barthélemy and ZZ for French citizens abroad.

examples.description: Français établis hors de France, 1re circonscription

ru.name: Код избирательного округа Национального собрания Франции

name: French municipality (commune)
doc: Name of a commune, the smallest administrative unit of France, for example Paris or Mende. Many names occur in more than one department, so a name alone does not identify a commune; its INSEE code (inseecode) does.

name: French department (département)
doc: Name of a department of France, the administrative level between the region and the commune, for example Ain or Corse-du-Sud. France has 101 departments, five of them overseas. The INSEE code of a department is the pattern fr_department_code.

patterns.name: French department code (INSEE)
patterns.doc: Code of a French department in the INSEE Official Geographic Code (COG). Departments in metropolitan France use two characters from 01 to 95, with 2A (Corse-du-Sud) and 2B (Haute-Corse) in place of 20. Overseas departments use three digits, 971 to 974 and 976.

name: French department code (INSEE)
doc: Code of a French department in the INSEE Official Geographic Code (COG). Departments in metropolitan France use two characters from 01 to 95, with 2A (Corse-du-Sud) and 2B (Haute-Corse) in place of 20. Overseas departments use three digits, 971 to 974 and 976.

name: French driver's license number
doc: Number of a driving licence issued in France. Microsoft Purview looks for twelve digits.

name: French FANTOIR street identifier
doc: Identifier of a street, locality (lieu-dit), housing estate or pseudo-street in FANTOIR, the file of streets and localities of the French tax administration (DGFiP), which TOPO replaced in July 2023. It has ten characters and a check letter: the department and direction code (3 characters, such as 450, 2A0, 754 or 971), the INSEE code of the commune within the department (3 digits), the RIVOLI code of the street (4 characters) and the RIVOLI key, as in 450 002 3086 F. The first character of the RIVOLI code tells the kind of way: a digit for a street, A for a housing estate or condominium, B to W for a locality (lieu-dit), X for a pseudo-street such as a canal or a metro station, Y or Z for a provisional street.

examples.description: Example from the DGFiP description of the FANTOIR file
The same identifier as printed in that description

Rue Beaubourg, an example of Wikidata P3182

name: French health and social establishment number (FINESS)
doc: Nine-character number of a legal entity or an establishment in FINESS, the French national register of health, medico-social and social establishments, managed by the Agence du Numérique en Santé. The register gives a FINESS juridique number to each legal entity and a FINESS géographique number to each of its establishments (places of activity). The characters are digits, except that the second may be A or B.

examples.description: Assistance Publique - Hôpitaux de Paris, an example of Wikidata P4058
Hospital of the Groupe hospitalier Est Réunion, an example of Wikidata P4058

name: French health insurance card number
doc: Number of the French health insurance card (carte Vitale). Microsoft Purview looks for 21 digits in groups of ten, ten and one.

name: French IRIS code (INSEE)
doc: Code of an IRIS, the basic sub-municipal unit of INSEE statistics. It has 9 characters - the 5-character code of the commune (of the municipal arrondissement in Paris, Lyon and Marseille) followed by 4 digits. A commune that is not divided into IRIS counts as one IRIS with the suffix 0000.

name: French activity code (NAF rév. 2 subclass, APE code)
doc: Code of a subclass of the French classification of activities NAF rév. 2 (2008), which has the same structure as the European NACE. INSEE gives every company and establishment in the SIRENE register an APE code (activité principale exercée) taken from it, so the APE code is also called the NAF code. A subclass code has four digits and a letter, usually written with a dot after the second digit, as in 79.11Z; data sets often leave the dot out. From 1 January 2027 APE codes are assigned from NAF 2025 instead.

name: French establishment number (NIC)
doc: Numéro interne de classement (NIC), the last 5 digits of a SIRET number. It tells apart the establishments of one legal unit identified by its SIREN and carries no information about activity or location. Its last digit is a check digit for the whole SIRET, so the NIC alone cannot be validated. Sirene files keep it in its own column, for example nicSiegeUniteLegale for the head office.

name: French tax identification number (numéro fiscal)
doc: Numéro fiscal de référence, also called NIF or SPI number, the 13-digit number that the French tax administration gives to each person who must report taxes. It starts with 0, 1, 2 or 3 and the last three digits are a check key.

The first example in its printed form

name: French occupation and socio-professional category code (PCS)
doc: Code in the INSEE nomenclature of professions and socio-professional categories (PCS). In PCS 2020 a group has 1 digit, a category 2 digits, a grouped profession 2 digits and a capital letter, and a profession 2 digits, a capital letter and a digit (37B5). In PCS 2003 a profession has 3 digits and a lowercase letter (372e). Public data often holds the 2-digit category.

ru.name: Код профессии и социально-профессиональной категории Франции (PCS)

name: French trade and companies register number (RCS)
doc: Registration of a trader or a commercial company in the French Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS), as written on its K or Kbis extract: RCS, the city of the registry, the letter A for an individual trader or B for a company, and the nine-digit SIREN number, as in RCS Nancy B 323 159 715. The check digit of the SIREN applies.

examples.description: The same number with a compact SIREN
Letter other than A or B

name: French region (région)
doc: Name of an administrative region of France, the level above the department, for example Île-de-France or Bretagne. France has 18 regions, five of them overseas. The INSEE code of a region is the pattern fr_region_code.

patterns.name: French region code (INSEE)
patterns.doc: Two-digit code of a French region in the INSEE Official Geographic Code (COG). The 18 current codes are 01 to 04 and 06 for the overseas regions and 11, 24, 27, 28, 32, 44, 52, 53, 75, 76, 84, 93 and 94 for the regions of metropolitan France.

name: French region code (INSEE)
doc: Two-digit code of a French region in the INSEE Official Geographic Code (COG). The 18 current codes are 01 to 04 and 06 for the overseas regions and 11, 24, 27, 28, 32, 44, 52, 53, 75, 76, 84, 93 and 94 for the regions of metropolitan France.

name: French RIVOLI street code
doc: Code of a street, locality or housing estate within its commune in the FANTOIR file of the French tax administration: the four-character RIVOLI code and its check letter, as in 3086F. It is the last part of the FANTOIR identifier (fr_fantoir) and is unique only within one commune. The first character of the RIVOLI code tells the kind of way: a digit for a street, A for a housing estate or condominium, B to W for a locality (lieu-dit), X for a pseudo-street such as a canal or a metro station, Y or Z for a provisional street.

name: French association number (RNA)
doc: Number of an association in the Répertoire national des associations (RNA), the register of associations declared under the 1901 law that the Ministry of the Interior keeps; it replaced the Waldec register in 2010. In metropolitan France it is the letter W and nine digits; Wikidata also accepts W followed by 2A or 2B, or by 9 and one of the letters G, M, C, T, R or N, and seven digits. Wikidata keeps numbers of the earlier register, such as 751P00105292, in a separate property (P6309). Associations of Alsace-Moselle law are not in the RNA.

name: French national building identifier (ID-RNB)
doc: Identifier of a building in the Référentiel National des Bâtiments (RNB), the French national register of buildings. It has 12 characters drawn at random from the digits 1 to 9 and the capital letters except I, L, O and U, so that it cannot be misread, and is often written in three groups of four separated by hyphens, as in W7WG-YK8D-C68P.

name: French employee headcount band (Sirene tranche d'effectifs)
doc: Two-character code of the band of salaried employees of a legal unit or establishment in the Sirene register (trancheEffectifsUniteLegale, trancheEffectifsEtablissement) - NN for units without employees, 00 for no employee, then bands from 01 (1 or 2) to 53 (10 000 and more). Older INSEE files used slightly different labels for 00 and 52.

name: French UAI code (school identifier)
doc: Code of a French educational establishment in the Répertoire national des établissements (RNE): seven digits and a check letter.

name: French urban unit code (INSEE unité urbaine)
doc: Five-character code of an unité urbaine, an INSEE zoning of built-up areas (continuous buildings with at least 2,000 inhabitants). Files name the columns uu2020 or uu2010 after the zoning year; communes outside any urban unit can carry a special value instead of a code.

doc: French vehicle license plate by field name

name: French employment zone code (INSEE zone d'emploi)
doc: Code of a zone d'emploi, an INSEE zoning that groups communes where most residents both live and work. The 2020 zoning replaced the 2010 one; files name the columns ze2020 or ze2010. The format of the code is not checked here.

name: French cadastral reference by field name
doc: French cadastral reference by field name identifier

name: French national identity card
doc: The French national identity card (CNI) is an official identity document consisting of an electronic ID-1 card bearing a photograph, name and address.

name: Freebase machine ID (MID)
doc: Identifier of a topic in Freebase, the knowledge base that Google shut down in 2016: /m/0 followed by lowercase letters, digits and underscores. Google Knowledge Graph and many datasets still use these identifiers.

name: French full name of the person
doc: Full name of the person written in French

name: French social security number (NIR)
doc: French national identification number (numéro d'inscription au répertoire, NIR), known as the social security number. INSEE assigns it to every person born in France. It has 13 characters and a two-digit control key: sex (1 or 2; 7 or 8 for temporary registrations), year and month of birth, department and commune of birth (2A or 2B for Corsica), an order number, and the key. The key is 97 minus the 13-character number modulo 97, with 2A read as 19 and 2B as 18.

EU social security number or equivalent identification

doc: Number of French passport

name: French postal code
doc: French postal code

name: French property number by field name
doc: French property number by field name identifier

name: French VAT number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire)
doc: Numéro de TVA intracommunautaire, the VAT identification number of businesses in France: FR, a 2-character key and the 9-digit SIREN number of the business. In older numbers the key is two digits computed from the SIREN; in newer numbers at least one character of the key is a letter, never I or O. Businesses in Monaco receive numbers of the same form (see mc_tva).

name: BBC Programme Identifier (PID)
doc: Persistent identifier of a BBC television or radio programme brand, series or episode, used in BBC web addresses, iPlayer and internal systems. It is a lower-case letter followed by seven or more lower-case consonants or digits; vowels are never used. The first letter shows the issuing source, for example b or p. Most PIDs have eight characters; some World Service programmes have eleven.

name: BBFC age rating (United Kingdom)
doc: Age rating of a film, video or online programme by the British Board of Film Classification: U (universal), PG (parental guidance), 12A (cinema films: 12 and over, younger children with an adult), 12 (videos: 12 and over), 15, 18 and R18 (restricted, sold only in licensed shops). Uc (universal, particularly suitable for young children) was used for videos until 2009.

name: UK community amateur sports club identifier (CASC)
doc: Identifier of a community amateur sports club (CASC) registered with HM Revenue and Customs, as published in the CASC list that ORG-ID.guide enhanced with unique identifiers. ORG-ID.guide lists the register as GB-CASC; with that prefix an identifier reads GB-CASC-df679063.

name: Registered charity number (England and Wales)
doc: Number of a charity in the register of the Charity Commission for England and Wales. ORG-ID.guide lists the register as GB-CHC; with that prefix an identifier reads GB-CHC-279417.

name: Church of England church code
doc: Code of a church or other body in the church codes of the Church of England. ORG-ID.guide lists the register as GB-COE; with that prefix an identifier reads GB-COE-608393.

name: United Kingdom county
doc: Name of a county or a similar area of the United Kingdom, such as Kent, Greater Manchester, Aberdeenshire or Antrim. Lists mix ceremonial, historic and administrative counties with Scottish council areas.

name: UK electoral roll number
doc: Elector number on the electoral register of the United Kingdom: a two-letter polling district code followed by one to four digits.

name: UK government department IATI reference number
doc: Reference number of a UK government department in the IATI version 2 codes for UK government bodies. ORG-ID.guide lists the register as GB-GOV; with that prefix an identifier reads GB-GOV-1.

name: HESA institution identifier (INSTID)
doc: INSTID, the identifier of a higher education provider that returns data to the Higher Education Statistics Agency (HESA) of the United Kingdom. ORG-ID.guide lists the register as GB-HESA; with that prefix an identifier reads GB-HESA-0177.

name: HMRC charity reference
doc: Reference that HM Revenue and Customs gives to a charity for tax purposes. ORG-ID.guide lists the register as GB-REV; with that prefix an identifier reads GB-REV-X6243.

name: UK local authority register code
doc: Three-letter code of a local authority in the local authority registers of the UK Government Digital Service for England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales. The codes follow the second part of the ISO 3166-2:GB subdivision codes where one exists. ORG-ID.guide lists it under GB-LAE, GB-LANI, GB-LAS and GB-PLA; with that prefix an identifier reads GB-LAE-WOT.

name: UK electricity Meter Point Administration Number (MPAN core)
doc: Meter Point Administration Number, also called the supply number, which identifies an exit point of the electricity network in Great Britain. The 13-digit core has a 2-digit distributor id, 10 digits for the meter point and a check digit: the first twelve digits are multiplied by the primes 3, 5, 7, 13, 17, 19, 23, 29, 31, 37, 41 and 43, and the sum modulo 11 modulo 10 is the check digit. On bills the core is preceded by a top line with the profile class, the meter time switch code and the line loss factor class, which together make the full 21-character number.

Synthetic core with a valid check digit

patterns.name: UK electricity MPAN, full 21-character form
patterns.doc: Full Meter Point Administration Number as printed on electricity bills in Great Britain, without the separating spaces: a 2-digit profile class (00 to 08), a 3-digit meter time switch code, a 3-character line loss factor class and the 13-digit MPAN core.

name: UK electricity MPAN, full 21-character form
doc: Full Meter Point Administration Number as printed on electricity bills in Great Britain, without the separating spaces: a 2-digit profile class (00 to 08), a 3-digit meter time switch code, a 3-character line loss factor class and the 13-digit MPAN core.

name: UK gas Meter Point Reference Number (MPRN)
doc: Meter Point Reference Number, also called the M number, which identifies a gas supply meter point in Great Britain. The gas transporter allocates it and Xoserve holds it in UK Link. National Grid documents it as 10 digits, the last two being check digits whose algorithm is not published. Suppliers also report shorter legacy numbers, which the regexp does not cover.

name: UK Mutuals Public Register number
doc: Registration number of a mutual society, such as a co-operative, a community benefit society or a credit union, in the Mutuals Public Register of the Financial Conduct Authority. ORG-ID.guide lists the register as GB-MPR; with that prefix an identifier reads GB-MPR-235C.

name: NHS Organisation Data Service code (ODS code)
doc: Code of an NHS or other health and social care organisation in the Organisation Data Service (ODS). ORG-ID.guide lists the register as GB-NHS; with that prefix an identifier reads GB-NHS-01F.

name: Northern Ireland registered charity number
doc: Number of a charity in the register of the Charity Commission for Northern Ireland. ORG-ID.guide lists the register as GB-NIC; with that prefix an identifier reads GB-NIC-100019.

name: Northern Ireland institution reference number
doc: Reference number (institution number) of a school or other institution in Schools Plus, the directory of the Department of Education of Northern Ireland. ORG-ID.guide lists the register as GB-IRN; with that prefix an identifier reads GB-IRN-542-0059.

name: Scottish charity number
doc: Number of a charity in the Scottish Charity Register. ORG-ID.guide lists the register as GB-SC; with that prefix an identifier reads GB-SC-SC042386.

name: Scottish school SEED code
doc: SEED code, the 7-digit identifier of a school or other education establishment in the Register of Schools of the Scottish Government. ORG-ID.guide lists the register as GB-SCOTEDU; with that prefix an identifier reads GB-SCOTEDU-8212627.

name: Registered social housing provider code (England)
doc: Registered provider code of a social housing provider in the statutory register of social housing providers in England. ORG-ID.guide lists the register as GB-SHPE; with that prefix an identifier reads GB-SHPE-LH4401.

name: UK Supplier Registration Service identifier
doc: Identifier that the UK Government Supplier Registration Service (Crown Commercial Service) gives to a registered organisation: a domain, a slash and a unique string. ORG-ID.guide lists the register as GB-SRS; with that prefix an identifier reads GB-SRS-sid4gov.cabinetoffice.gov.uk/tBq37PN7.

name: English unique pupil number (UPN)
doc: Unique Pupil Number, the 13-character code of a pupil in English state schools. It is a check letter, a 3-digit local authority number, a 4-digit school establishment number, two digits for the year of issue and a 3-digit serial number. Temporary numbers end with a letter.

name: UK VAT registration number
doc: VAT registration number of businesses in the United Kingdom and the Isle of Man. The standard form has nine digits with a weighted check, sometimes followed by a 3-digit branch code; government departments (GD) and health authorities (HA) have short 5-character numbers. Northern Ireland businesses use the XI prefix for trade with the EU.

name: GBIF taxon key
doc: Numeric key of a taxon in the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy of the Global Biodiversity Information Facility, used in occurrence data downloads. Wikidata keeps the taxon identifiers of the taxonomy that GBIF introduced in 2026, which are short alphanumeric codes, in a separate property (P14607).

doc: GS1 identification key for a coupon offer, used on paper and digital coupons. Thirteen digits (a GS1 Company Prefix, a coupon reference and a GS1 check digit) may be followed by a serial component of up to 12 digits that identifies one issued coupon. In barcodes it is carried by Application Identifier (255); the element string is the pattern gs1_ai_255.

name: Global Document Type Identifier (GDTI)
doc: GS1 identification key for a type of document, such as a certificate, an invoice form or a permit. Thirteen digits (a GS1 Company Prefix, a document type and a GS1 check digit) may be followed by a serial component of up to 17 characters of GS1 character set 82 that identifies one document of that type. In barcodes it is carried by Application Identifier (253); the element string is the pattern gs1_ai_253.

name: Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) accession
doc: Accession of a record in the Gene Expression Omnibus, the NCBI repository of gene expression and other functional genomics data. The prefix gives the kind of record: GSE for a series (usually one study), GSM for a sample, GPL for a platform and GDS for a curated dataset; digits follow.

name: Opendatasoft geographic point (geo_point_2d)
doc: Geographic point stored in the geo_point_2d field type of the Opendatasoft data platform (now Huwise), which runs many French and other European open data portals. Datasets often keep the default field name geo_point_2d, usually next to a geo_shape field with the full geometry of the record. The point is a latitude and a longitude in decimal degrees. The Explore API v2.1 returns it as a JSON object with lon and lat members. CSV exports write the latitude, a comma and a space, then the longitude, and the legacy Records API v1 returns a [latitude, longitude] array. This latitude-first order is the opposite of GeoJSON.

name: Opendatasoft geographic shape (geo_shape)
doc: Geometry stored in the geo_shape field type of the Opendatasoft data platform (now Huwise), which runs many French and other European open data portals. Datasets often keep the default field name geo_shape, usually next to a geo_point_2d field with a point of the same record. The value is GeoJSON, so positions are longitude first, then latitude. The Explore API v2.1 returns a GeoJSON Feature whose geometry member holds the shape and whose properties member is empty. CSV exports write the bare geometry object instead. One value holds one geometry of any GeoJSON type, such as Point, LineString, Polygon or MultiPolygon.

name: Geohash
doc: Geohash, a geocode invented by Gustavo Niemeyer in 2008. It interleaves the bits of longitude and latitude and writes them in a base-32 alphabet of digits and lowercase letters without a, i, l and o. Each added character makes the rectangle smaller, and codes with a common prefix are usually close to each other. The regexp allows 1 to 12 characters, the precision range of common implementations such as Elasticsearch; short values look like ordinary words and numbers.

name: GeoJSON geometry
doc: Geometry, feature or feature collection written in GeoJSON (RFC 7946), the JSON format for geographic data. Positions are longitude first, then latitude, in WGS 84.

name: GeoJSON geometry type
doc: Value of the type member of a GeoJSON geometry object. RFC 7946 defines seven case-sensitive geometry types - Point, MultiPoint, LineString, MultiLineString, Polygon, MultiPolygon and GeometryCollection. Tabular datasets often keep it in a column next to the coordinates, for example geoData.type in the datasets of the Moscow open data portal.

doc: Personal ID Number on the Ghana Card, issued by the National Identification Authority. Since April 2021 it is also the taxpayer identification number of individuals. It has three parts separated by hyphens: a three-letter country code of the holder's nationality at first registration (GHA for citizens), an 8- or 9-digit number and a check character, a digit or a letter, whose algorithm is not published.

The characters are random and come from the set 23456789cfghjmpqrvwx, always in lower case. An advisory that has a CVE identifier keeps its GHSA ID as well; OSV.dev also uses GHSA IDs as entry ids.

name: Global Individual Asset Identifier (GIAI)
doc: GS1 identification key for one asset that a company owns or uses, such as a machine, a computer or an aircraft part. It is a GS1 Company Prefix followed by an individual asset reference, up to 30 characters of GS1 character set 82 in total; the first four characters are digits because the shortest GS1 Company Prefix has four. Application Identifier (8004) carries it, and (7023) carries the GIAI of an assembly; the element strings are the patterns gs1_ai_8004 and gs1_ai_7023.

It is a GS1 Company Prefix followed by a consignment reference, up to 30 characters of GS1 character set 82 in total; the first four characters are digits because the shortest GS1 Company Prefix has four. name: GMDN term code
doc: Five-digit code of a generic device term in the Global Medical Device Nomenclature, maintained by the GMDN Agency. Each term has a name, a definition and a code; regulators and UDI databases such as the FDA GUDID record the code. Collective term codes are a different scheme and are not covered.

name: GML object identifier (gml:id)
doc: Value of the gml:id attribute, the handle of an object in a Geography Markup Language (GML) document, such as a feature or a geometry in a WFS response. Its XML Schema type is ID, so the value is an XML NCName (it starts with a letter or an underscore and has no colon or space) and it is unique only within the document that contains it. It serves internal cross-references and is not a persistent identifier; GML carries stable identifiers in gml:identifier instead. GeoServer builds it from the feature type name and a number, as in states.1. GDAL reads the attribute into a string field called gml_id, so tables exported from GML or WFS data with ogr2ogr or QGIS keep it as a column. The regexp covers the NCName characters of the Basic Multilingual Plane.

name: Global Model Number (GMN)
doc: GS1 identification key for a product model: the design that a group of trade items is made to. It is a GS1 Company Prefix, a model reference and two check characters, up to 25 characters of GS1 character set 82. The check character pair is computed from the other characters with prime weights modulo 1021. In barcodes it is carried by Application Identifier (8013); the element string is the pattern gs1_ai_8013.

name: Guinean permanent tax identification number (NIFp)
doc: Numéro d'Identification Fiscale Permanent, the tax number of taxpayers in Guinea issued by the Direction Générale des Impôts. It has nine digits, usually written as three groups separated by hyphens. The first eight digits are assigned pseudorandomly and the ninth is a Luhn check digit.

name: Guinea postal code

name: GND ID (Integrated Authority File of the German National Library)
doc: Identifier of a record in the Gemeinsame Normdatei (GND), the authority file for persons, corporate bodies, places, subjects and works kept by the German National Library and library networks in German-speaking countries. In 2012 it replaced the separate name (PND), corporate body (GKD) and subject heading (SWD) authority files. GND IDs come in several formats; the last character is a check character, a digit or X, and in some formats a hyphen precedes it.

name: GNS Unique Feature Identifier (UFI)
doc: Number of a place in the GEOnet Names Server of the US National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, which covers geographic names outside the United States. Some values are negative numbers.

name: Gene Ontology term ID
doc: Identifier of a term in the Gene Ontology, which describes molecular functions, cellular components and biological processes: GO: and seven digits.

name: Google API key
doc: API key for Google Cloud and Google Maps APIs: the prefix AIza followed by 35 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores.

name: Google Knowledge Graph ID
doc: Identifier of an entity in the Google Knowledge Graph that did not come from Freebase: /g/ followed by letters and digits. Entities that came from Freebase keep their /m/ identifiers.

name: Personal account for government budgets (Russian Treasury)
doc: A personal account is an account for use by an individual for that persons own needs. It is a relative term to differentiate them from those accounts for business or corporate use. Used by Russian treasury for organizations accounts.

name: Generic Public Subscription Identifier (GPSI) of a 5G network
doc: Public identifier of a 5G subscription that is used outside the 3GPP system, unlike the SUPI (3GPP TS 23.003). The service APIs of the 5G core (3GPP TS 29.571) write it as msisdn- followed by an MSISDN, or extid- followed by an external identifier of the form local-id@domain.

name: Universally unique identifier (UUID)
doc: 128-bit identifier that systems generate without a central registry, defined by RFC 9562 (2024), which replaced RFC 4122. Microsoft calls it a GUID. The text form is 32 hexadecimal digits in five groups of 8, 4, 4, 4 and 12 separated by hyphens, in any letter case. The first digit of the third group is the version (1 to 8, see uuid_v1, uuid_v4 and uuid_v7), and the first digit of the fourth group is 8, 9, a or b for the RFC 9562 variant. The Nil UUID (all zeros) and the Max UUID (all f) are special values. Microsoft tools and the Windows registry write GUIDs in curly braces, a form the regexp also accepts. The regexp does not accept the 32 digits without hyphens, which look like an MD5 hash, or the urn:uuid form (uuid_urn).

patterns.name: UUID as a URN (urn:uuid)
patterns.doc: A UUID written as a URN in the uuid namespace, urn:uuid:<UUID>, as RFC 9562 defines. It is used where an identifier must be a URI, for example as the id of Atom feeds and entries (RFC 4287), in RDF data and as the identifier of EPUB packages. The urn and uuid parts are case-insensitive.

name: H3 cell index
doc: Index of a cell (hexagon or pentagon) of H3, the hierarchical hexagonal grid system developed at Uber. The 64-bit index holds the index mode (1 for a cell), the resolution from 0 to 15, one of 122 base cells and one digit from 0 to 6 for each finer resolution; unused digits are set to 7. The canonical text form is lowercase hexadecimal without padding or prefix, so a cell index has 15 characters, starts with 8, and its second character is the resolution. H3 directed edge and vertex indexes use other modes and are not covered.

name: German commercial register number (Handelsregisternummer)
doc: Number of an entry in the German commercial register (Handelsregister), which the local courts (Amtsgerichte) keep. It is the register section and a number of up to six digits: HRA for sole traders and partnerships such as OHG and KG, HRB for corporations such as GmbH and AG. Some courts add a letter suffix, as in HRB 12345 B. The cooperative (GnR), partnership (PR) and association (VR) registers number their entries the same way. A number is unique only together with the court, as in Amtsgericht München HRB 123456. HRA entries can name natural persons (sole traders).

The regexp matches handles with a dotted prefix; older handles with a single numeric prefix such as 2381/12345 cannot be told apart from other slash-separated values by their form.
